meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (French Code Civil heritage, German doctrinal influence, EU acquis)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–United States Income and Capital Taxation Convention (signed 3 April 1996, as amended by the 2009 Protocol)
Luxembourg–China Double Taxation Agreement (signed 12 March 1983, as amended by the 2019 Protocol)
Luxembourg–United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (1967, as amended)
Belgium–Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) Bilateral Investment Treaty with the People's Republic of China (signed 2005, in force 2009)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (inter alia by the Law of 25 January 2021 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs, RBE), as amended following the CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022 (joined cases C-37/20 and C-601/20); Grand-Ducal implementing regulations on the RBE; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on central administration, internal governance and risk management; Luxembourg Criminal Code Articles 506-1 et seq. on money laundering; FATF Recommendations and EU AML Directives 2015/849 and 2018/843 as incorporated into Luxembourg law.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / commercial-register extract of every foreign corporate partner or shareholder (e.g., Delaware LLC, BVI or Cayman holding vehicle)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or Secretary of State in the country of origin of the foreign entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961), plus certified French translation; consular legalization only for non-Hague signatory jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport / national ID and residential proof of each beneficial owner and of the general partner (commandité)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registry or passport authority of the individual's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certified-copy certificate followed by Hague Apostille; consular legalization where the origin country is not a Hague Contracting State

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate / criminal-record extract (extrait de casier judiciaire) of each manager and of the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Justice or national police authority of the country of residence (in Luxembourg: Ministère de la Justice)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus sworn translation into French or German for attachment to the notarial file

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and documentary evidence of source of funds for the initial partner contributions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Credit institution of the partner's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostilled original or consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions; bank seals and signatures certified by a notary

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 16-1 to 16-40 (SCSp regime, inserted by the Law of 12 July 2013), read with the Law of 19 December 2008 on the Luxembourg Business Registers and applicable Civil Code partnership provisions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), e-filing via MyGuichet
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for RCS registration (LR form) together with the signed SCSp limited partnership agreement (contrat de société / limited partnership agreement) and registered office declaration
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum statutory or paid-up capital applies to an SCSp. Contributions are freely fixed in the LPA and may be cash, in-kind or a mix; no notarial escrow or blocked capital account is required, except that a real-estate contribution must be executed before a notary and, if cash is contributed, payment is evidenced by bank account records of the SCSp.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: UNANIMOUS MANAGING PARTNER RESOLUTION. The Manager, being the sole General Partner of [SCSp Name] SCSp, resolves: (1) The Subscription Notice and contribution schedule attached to the LPA are approved; all admitted Limited Partners' interests are accepted. (2) The registered office is adopted at [street address], Luxembourg, and all official service of process shall be received there. (3) [Name] is appointed Manager/Administrateur and [Name] is appointed authorized signatory, each acting singly, with authority to file RCS registration, open bank accounts and represent the SCSp before tax and social authorities. (4) This resolution is effective immediately and shall be filed with the RCS. Signed at [place], [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of SCSp limited partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public if real property is contributed; otherwise the founding partners directly, with subsequent transmission to the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the LPA containing the legal form SCSp, the company name, corporate object covering creator incubation and MCN talent representation, duration, registered office address, identities of partners, classes of partnership interests, general partner management powers, contribution schedule, distribution rules, transfer restrictions and dissolution clauses. Execute by private deed where possible or by notarial deed where real estate is contributed. Legalise or apostille signatures of non-Luxembourg resident persons if requested.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of each general and limited partner
Proposed limited partnership agreement or notarial deed
Notarization, legalization or apostille of foreign signature documents if applicable
Draft registered-office declaration or approved domiciliation agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the LPA is objected to by the RCS, execute a private supplementary agreement signed by all partners correcting the contested clauses; re-submission to the RCS may accept the original deed together with the addendum unless re-notarization is imposed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - RCS (pre-registration consultation via MyGuichet)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the proposed company name against existing RCS entries, protected designations and trademarks. The name must include SCSp or a clear equivalent. Terms suggesting banking, insurance or sovereign functions require additional authorizations. Submit a name-check request with the draft LPA. If the name is available, proceed immediately to formal registration within the validity window.
required_dossiers: Signed or draft LPA
Name verification request form
Power of attorney if filing is made by a professional
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, propose up to three alternative names; the LBR will reserve one, and the LPA must be amended by addendum before the registration application is filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), electronically through MyGuichet
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of signing the LPA, submit the RCS application together with a certified copy of the executed deed, registered-office acceptance, identity proof of the general partner and powers of attorney. Pay the RCS filing fee online. If the LPA is drafted in English only, attach a certified French or German translation for the RCS record. The LBR will examine the application and issue the RCS registration extract.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the signed or notarial LPA
RCS LR application form
Registered-office consent or declaration from landlord or domiciliation agent
Certified translation into French or German if the LPA is in English
Power of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: RCS observations must be remedied within 15 calendar days through MyGuichet; where that deadline is missed, file a fresh LR application with an explanatory note and observe the late-filing regime and possible administrative penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - RCS publication in the RESA official electronic compilation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, the LBR automatically publishes the required legal particulars in the RESA, including the legal form, name, registered office, partner liability and sole-general-partner identity. Verify the published entry for exact spelling of the name, address and officer details and retain the RCS publication excerpt for banking and tax uses.
required_dossiers: RCS registration number and filing receipt
Approved LPA excerpt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA entry contains errors, file a rectification request with the LBR attaching supporting evidence; the original publication date remains valid and the corrected entry is linked to the original filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes and Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA, both accessible via MyGuichet / guichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, apply for the Luxembourg national registration number and, where relevant, the common-VAT number. Complete the direct-tax file for the SCSp. If the SCSp is tax-transparent, the general partner reports income and the VAT position follows the partnership; VAT registration should be made when taxable supplies exceed the threshold or where the MCN needs to recover input VAT. Attach the RCS extract and the executed LPA.
required_dossiers: RCS extract
General partner or manager passport
Executed LPA or notarial deed
Proof of registered office
AEDT business or VAT registration application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax registry queries the application, provide the requested translations or notarized copies within the deadline; where late VAT registration has occurred, file a supplementary application with an explanation and current outstanding return schedules to mitigate penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social security registration and occupational safety declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Inspection du Travail et des Mines for workplace clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp as an employer with the CCSS when any salaried manager, employee or intern is engaged. File the occupational health and safety declaration with the Labour and Mines Inspectorate and keep a workplace description at the registered office. If the MCN uses only independent creators through service contracts, no employment registration is triggered, but the general partner must still confirm the applicable social-security status.
required_dossiers: RCS extract
General partner identification document
Employment contracts or standard creator-service agreement template
Workplace address, floor plan and emergency plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CCSS queries missing staff data, respond through the dedicated online channel within 10 working days; for labour-inspectorate observations, submit a corrective action plan and request a re-inspection within 10 working days after remedial works.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable. No sector-specific industrial licence is required for ISIC 7310 / creator-MCN agency activity under Luxembourg law. Where physical premises are occupied, the municipal administration verifies only ordinary building and town-planning compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating licence required - freedom of establishment applies; no commercial establishment authorisation under the Luxembourg Law of 2 September 2011 on access to regulated craft, commercial and industrial professions is needed for talent representation and MCN services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement - Ministère de l'Environnement, du Climat et du Développement durable
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / no mandatory EIA registration. An SCSp operating an office-based creator incubator and MCN agency does not carry out an industrial installation listed in the Luxembourg environmental impact assessment annex.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC or industrial-emission thresholds apply to office-only premises. Any incidental canteen wastewater must comply with municipal sewer discharge rules; electronic-waste arising from streaming or production equipment must be collected under the Luxembourg waste-management regulations; stationary cooling equipment using fluorinated greenhouse gases must comply with EU Regulation 517/2014 and national energy decrees.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection by the municipal fire service and the Service d'Incendie et de Secours is required for any office, studio or production space ordinarily open to employees or public visitors; structural-load clearance is recommended for studio equipment installations; a workplace-safety declaration under the Labour Code must be filed with the Labour and Mines Inspectorate before personnel are engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) is the Luxembourg VAT and registration authority; income tax is administered by Administration des contributions directes (ACD). Official portals: guichet.lu / myguichet.lu, www.aedt.public.lu; VAT filing portal: eTVA/eCDF.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident investor establishing an SCSp must first file the SCSp partnership agreement and register the SCSp with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) if it engages in commercial activity, obtaining an RCS registration number; simultaneously, a Luxembourg national tax identification number (matricule) is issued by the ACD/RCS system. To become a VAT taxable person, file Form 564 (VAT registration application) with the AEDT through the eCDF portal or by letter, attaching the RCS extract, partnership deed, evidence of economic activity (TikTok/MCN contracts, bank details, GP identity), and, if the SCSp has no Luxembourg seat, the appointment of an approved Luxembourg VAT representative. The AEDT then issues a Luxembourg VAT number in the format 'LU' + 8 digits, together with an ERP (registered exporter/taxpayer) number for the eTVA filing account. A non-EU entity without an establishment must appoint a fiscal representative unless it can use the OSS/import VAT mechanism.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: There is no general check-the-box election under Luxembourg law; SCSp tax transparency for direct income tax purposes is mandatory and not elective. The SCSp may elect, for a specific commercial/regulated fund structure, to be organized under the RAIF Law or the UCI Law, which changes the regulatory but not the VAT direct treatment. Under ATAD, hybrid mismatch elections are restricted: the SCSp cannot be simultaneously transparent and opaque in different EU jurisdictions for Luxembourg tax purposes without adjustment. For US federal tax classification only, an SCSp may file Form 8832 to elect its classification as a partnership or disregarded entity; Form 8858 is then used for reporting the foreign partnership or disregarded entity. Luxembourg will generally respect the SCSp's pass-through status for Luxembourg income tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA/VAT), governed by the Luxembourg VAT Law (LTVL) and EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 30,000 annual taxable turnover (excluding VAT) for the Luxembourg small-enterprise franchise/exemption; above that threshold Luxembourg-established suppliers must register for VAT. Non-established foreign suppliers have no minimum turnover threshold and are required to register in Luxembourg or use the OSS/reverse-charge mechanism for supplies where Luxembourg VAT is due, subject to place-of-supply rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping applies. Luxembourg permits e-invoicing for B2B with customer consent and requires suppliers to the public sector to issue compliant e-invoices through Peppol BIS (EU Directive 2014/55/EU). VAT returns and recapitulative statements (VIES) are filed electronically through eCDF/eTVA; continuous transaction controls, SAF-T filing, and real-time digital reporting are not currently mandatory, although they may be requested during audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported outside the EU may be taxed at 0% VAT, provided the exporter holds valid transport/export documentation proving the goods left Luxembourg and the EU within the legal time limits. Services supplied by the Luxembourg MCN agency to a non-EU business customer such as TikTok or a foreign creator-operator are generally outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT if the B2B place-of-supply test places the supply where the customer is established; no Luxembourg VAT is charged and no export zero-rating declaration is required, but evidence of the customer's non-EU status must be kept. Electronically supplied services such as digital creator management, advertising, licensing and monetisation-platform services supplied to non-EU B2B customers also qualify for outside-scope treatment; supplies to EU consumers may be reported through the OSS and taxed in the consumer's member state, subject to the EUR 10,000 Union threshold rules for cross-border digital services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document, SAD/export declaration lodged with Luxembourg or exit customs)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / CMR consignment note evidencing physical dispatch outside the EU
Commercial invoice / tax invoice containing export zero-rating statement and Incoterms
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/MT103 bank credit voucher proving the export proceeds are received and identifiable
Place-of-supply evidence for MCN agency services: signed contract, customer VAT number or non-EU residency proof, IP/licence evidence, and service delivery records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may retrospectively disallow export zero-rating or outside-scope treatment if the export evidence trail is incomplete, contradictions exist between the customs declaration and invoice/payment documents, or the exporter fails to prove dispatch outside the EU. The clawback reassesses Luxembourg VAT at 17% plus statutory late interest and can extend to unlawful input VAT deduction reversals. Fraudulent submission of false export certificates or fictitious outward dispatches may trigger administrative fines generally up to EUR 25,000 per offence, criminal penalties under the Luxembourg Criminal Code and Customs and Excise Code including imprisonment, debarment from beneficial VAT regimes, and joint liability of the taxable person and any authorised representative. The regular VAT audit limitation period is five years, extending to ten years where fraud or deliberate omission is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) holds monetary authority and balance-of-payments statistical reporting competence within the Eurosystem; the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) is the competent banking regulator and AML/CFT supervisor, jointly with BCL for systemic payments oversight. Luxembourg maintains no foreign-exchange control institution nor capital-control decree; EU free movement of capital under TFEU Articles 63–66 prevails.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Capital-account convertibility is unrestricted for EU cross-border flows and for third-country flows subject to EU sanctions, FATF counter-measures, and the general anti-abuse doctrine. Profit remittances and distributions from a Luxembourg SCSp are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax; non-resident partners relieve through treaty or domestic pass-through rules. The practical hurdles are documentary: banks demand RBE-controller statements, CRS self-certifications, and proof that the SCSp is not a de-facto regulated AIF. Current-account payments for creator commissions and advertising services are unrestricted, but the payor must screen all counterparties against EU/UN sanctions lists and report suspicious transactions to the CRF (Cellule de Renseignements Financiers) where required by the Law of 12 November 2004 on AML/CFT, as amended.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no domiciliation-of-receipts requirement exist for export proceeds in Luxembourg. Receipts from non-resident TikTok/MCN contract counterparties may be kept freely in any currency. However, mandatory statistical reporting applies under BCL Regulation 2002/143 and BCL Circulars on external statistics: any direct-investment flow, including capital contributions from non-resident partners or intercompany treasury movements, must be declared to the BCL Centre de Déclarations on a per-transaction or aggregated monthly basis where the threshold (generally EUR 12,500 per transaction or per counterparty cumulative within the month) is met. Such declarations can be delegated to the account-holding bank; failure to file is an administrative offence. No special invoice collection or FX repatriation deadline exists for advertising/creator-management services.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium. Wise B2B, holding an EMI licence from the National Bank of Belgium passported via the EEA regime, can service a Luxembourg-registered SCSp in principle, but the SCSp's absence of legal personality creates onboarding friction: the EMI must complete a contractual-document review of the partnership agreement, RBE extract, and the General Partner's corporate KYC. Legal constraints: (i) the SCSp cannot contract in its own name where the contract is executed by the General Partner; (ii) most EMIs mandate one natural-person ultimate beneficial owner holding ≥25%; (iii) the commercial-payer exemption under PSD2 Article 3(b) shields the MCN agency from payment-institution licensing only if creator payouts fall strictly within its own commercial model, which a mass payout of thousands of creator commissions may challenge; outsourcing disbursements to a licensed PSP (Wise/Payoneer) preserves the exemption. High-volume USD creator payouts suggest pairing an EMI with a Tier-1 correspondent-capable bank for the SCSp's primary treasury account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory rule mandates in-person appearance under CSSF AML circulars or the Law of 12 November 2004, as amended; video-identification and e-signature are legally acceptable. In de facto bank practice for a Luxembourg SCSp — which lacks legal personality and acts through its General Partner — at least one physical presence session is required either at the bank or at a notary for (i) the General Partner's authorised managers, and (ii) any natural-person founder/UBO holding >25%. BGL BNP Paribas and BIL permit remote onboarding only where a Luxembourg-regulated Professional of the Financial Sector (PFS) or a notary certifies identity and opted-into-compliance; otherwise the branch compliance officer insists on a face-to-face interview. Budget for a physical trip to Luxembourg for the GP manager and, if applicable, the lead LP founder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp lacks separate legal personality; the bank cannot establish who legally owns and controls the account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCS) registration certificate and latest extract; notarised partnership agreement (contrat de société) including the SCSp statute; irrevocable Power of Attorney granted to the General Partner; board resolution of the General Partner appointing the account signatories; RBE extract (beneficial ownership register); corporate chart of the General Partner and all partners holding directly or indirectly ≥25% of partnership interests.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ambiguity on the tax/regulatory status of the SCSp: whether the vehicle is a collective investment undertaking (AIF/sub-threshold AIF) or purely commercial.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written legal opinion from a Luxembourg law firm (Arendt & Medernach, Loyens & Loeff or Elvinger Hoss) confirming the SCSp is a commercial operating partnership outside the 2013 AIFM law; executed agreements with TikTok/MCN creators evidencing the commercial agency activity; management accounts or budget showing operating substance; anti-money-laundering policy and risk assessment if internalised.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for inbound capital injection from non-resident partners (e.g., US/Asia founders) fails bank's provenance verification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of bank statements of the contributor; wealth statement and tax confirmation for each contributing partner; closing statements of the previous business sale or accrued salary/creator revenue documentation; notarised contribution resolutions; contract underlying the MCN business (TikTok/creator agreements) demonstrating commercial reason for the injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume outbound creator payouts to dozens of non-resident beneficiaries trigger payment-institution, terrorist financing and trade-sanctions flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Standardised commission agreements with global creators; KYC file of each material creator/beneficiary (name, date of birth, passport, tax ID) from an outreach dashboard; sanctions-screening evidence (EU/UN/OFAC) at onboarding and continuous transaction monitoring; MLRO (Money Laundering Reporting Officer) designation and annual compliance report; outsourcing agreements with regulated PSPs (Wise B2B, Payoneer) confirming the PSP performs transaction-level screening; negative opinion from a counsel confirming the commercial-payer exemption under PSD2 Article 3(b).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: CRS/FATCA classification and tax-transparency impediments: the SCSp is a pass-through entity; the bank needs self-certifications for each partner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CRS Form 1030 / CRS self-certification of the entity and Forms 6166, W-8BEN-E or W-9 for each direct partner; a side letter from the Luxembourg tax administration confirming the partnership's non-resident partner treatment; consolidated tax transparency opinion describing the pass-through into each partner jurisdiction; flow chart of the chain from partners to SCSp to bank accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital of the SCSp is zero or minimal (no minimum capital requirement), causing banks to doubt viability and commercial substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cash flow projection for twelve months from creator-management commissions; committed capital support letter or shareholders' undertaking from the General Partner; operating budget including Luxembourg staff, registered office and PFS expenses; existing executed TikTok/US-based creator agency contracts evidencing projected ARR to justify the treasury activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire routing for the initial capital contribution and subsequent shareholder loans: the remitting partner transmits via SWIFT MT103 from their home bank to the Luxembourg account at BGL BNP Paribas/BIL with the SCSp's full legal name, LEI (if available) and Luxembourg seat in field 57A and 59, and an ISO 20022 ExternalPurpose code of EQUI for equity contribution or INTC for intercompany advances; the memo must separately cite the partnership agreement article and the RBE registration date. For EUR injections originating inside SEPA, a SEPA Credit Transfer with purpose code EQUI is acceptable. For USD injections, the MT103 must clear via the bank's USD clearing account, and the bank will request a source-of-funds declaration, the contribution resolution, and updated RBE. If the injection subsequently requires statistical filings, the account bank applies the BoP threshold rule (EUR 12,500) on behalf of the SCSp; otherwise a BCL direct-investment declaration through the Centre de Déclarations must be filed. Crediting to a dedicated Capital Escrow Account is recommended until the contribution is verified; conversion into EUR from USD is done via a spot contract to avoid a floating exposure.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail for creator commission and licence fee disbursements is SWIFT MT103 corporate wire using current-account funds; intra-EU/EEA creator payouts are executed via SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant (up to the EUR 100,000 per-transaction ceiling). Commercial Letters of Credit are inapplicable to the MCN/advertising services model and should not be opened; such LC usage would require presentation of transport documents contradicting the service-based export and would be treated as an AML/CFT anomaly. For mass cross-border micro-payouts (more than 1,000 low-value commissions), the bank should enable batch API host-to-host debiting of the SCSp account and disbursement via licensed PSP mass-payout rails (Wise B2B, Payoneer Payouts) which aggregate settlement to the beneficiary's local account in local currency, while the SCSp's core treasury remains in EUR; the PSP outsourcing agreement must define money segregatio, reconciliation intervals, and audit rights. Outbound payments must be screened against sanctions and payment purpose codes should use the appropriate commercial category (INTC for group payouts, CHAR or TRAD for creator commissions per counterparty agreement).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD FX forwards (plain vanilla, tenor ≤ 12 months) matched against TikTok USD-settled revenue, executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or a bank's FX line with credit support annex.
FX swaps (FX swap of principal/interest in EUR/USD) for managing short-dated liquidity between the cap-call date and payout runs.
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD fixed-for-floating or fixed-for-fixed) for long-duration deflation of USD-denominated creator payout exposures.

NDF contracts are permissible only if a specific creator-currency pair lacks a deliverable offshore market (e.g., certain Emerging-Asian restricted currencies); Luxembourg banks would usually trade them bilaterally with a recognised counterparty and they will be reported under EMIR; speculative NDFs are prohibited by internal treasury policy.
No crypto-currency hedging or digital-asset swaps are permissible without a specific CSSF crypto-asset service-provider licence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation (Confirmation Annuelle) of registered data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after each anniversary of the entity's initial registration in the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts an administrative fine of up to EUR 100; persistent default may lead to formal warning and administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts and audit report filing (if mandatory audit thresholds are met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year-end and before the annual confirmation deadline; filing within one month of approval is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance may result in court-imposed fines up to EUR 3,000 and, in the event of persistent default, court-ordered strike-off of the entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Owner (RBE) annual verification and post-change filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) – Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous obligation; any change requires filing within one month. Annual internal review must be evidenced by not later than one month after the RCS anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to refresh RBE data within one month of a change triggers fines from EUR 250 to EUR 1,250,000 depending on the nature and reiteration of the breach.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit is triggered when the SCSp exceeds two of the three size criteria on the balance sheet date for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average employees 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as set out in the Law of 10 August 1915 and amended; IFRS is mandatory only for entities with listed securities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: An annual confirmation cycle is conducted: each partner must certify in writing by no later than 31 December of each year that there has been no undisclosed change in the identity or country of tax residence of the partnership's beneficial owners. Where a transfer of partnership interests or any other change occurs, an RBE update must be filed within one month of the relevant transaction. The SCSp must also retain all annual confirmations in the corporate file for 7 years.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (combined top effective rate in Luxembourg City: 17% corporate income tax + 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The SCSp is fiscally transparent; no entity-level corporate income tax is levied on the partnership itself. Income is directly allocated to partners and taxed at partner level. Qualifying corporate partners may benefit from the Luxembourg participation exemption (100% exemption on dividends and capital gains from qualifying shareholdings), the 80% IP income exemption, the notional interest deduction, investment tax credits, and protective tax rulings. Tax holidays are generally not available. For the purposes of this compliance model, tax loss carryforward is fixed at five years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 5 (Partnership Income Tax Return) filed through the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration electronic portal 'eCDF' via MyGuichet.lu; corporate partners must report their share of SCSp income on Form 4 (Corporate Income Tax Return) using the same portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 May of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end; electronic filing before 31 July automatically extends the deadline to 31 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: matricule d'impôt (Luxembourg business registration number), RCS number, registered office, and fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must be identified by name, permanent address, foreign tax identification number, and country of residence; a tax representative resident in Luxembourg may be required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period start and end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the period matches the SCSp's audited or internally prepared accounts; non-resident partners should reconcile with their own tax-year calendars for flow-through allocations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross receipts from creator management: commissions, talent representation fees, TikTok creator payouts, platform incentives, advertising share, and sponsorship income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All revenue of the SCSp must be declared, including amounts received on behalf of non-resident creator partners. Non-resident partners are not permitted to omit revenue indirectly arising from their Luxembourg agency operations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses: creator advances, sub-agent fees, office rent, payroll, software subscriptions, professional services, and licensing costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be substantiated with invoices; cost apportionment among non-resident partners requires a written partnership allocation schedule attached to the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable result before allocation to partners: gross income minus deductible expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The net result must be allocated on a pro-rata basis according to each partner's share in the SCSp agreement. Non-resident partners should report this amount in their own tax filings under the applicable DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of taxable result to resident and non-resident partners, including each partner's Luxembourg identification or foreign tax number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a schedule detailing the percentage allocation, amounts, and tax residence country for each partner. A non-resident partner must attach a current Tax Resident Certificate (TRC) if claiming treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, prepayments, and withholding taxes suffered by the SCSp or its partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners may claim foreign tax credits in their residence state but must not double-claim Luxembourg credits unless the treaty so provides.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of related-party transactions and transfer pricing documentation status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State whether Local File and Master File thresholds are met; non-resident partners with transactions with the SCSp must provide a cross-border transfer pricing schedule.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an administrative fine of up to €2,500 and a 10% surcharge on the assessed tax; late payment accrues interest at 0.8% per month. Fraudulent omission can result in criminal fines up to €125,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (statutory Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends paid by resident companies; SCSp profit allocations are not dividends because the entity is fiscally transparent, so no withholding tax is imposed at the partnership level. A Luxembourg corporate partner may benefit from a 0% rate under the participation exemption or Parent-Subsidiary Directive)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident partner claiming reduced withholding or treaty relief must submit a valid Tax Resident Certificate (TRC) issued by the residence-state tax authorities, a signed Form 106 (application for reduced withholding tax or refund), and written confirmation of beneficial ownership to the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (ACD). The payer may apply the reduced treaty rate if the documentation is provided before distribution; otherwise, a refund claim must be filed within the statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Under Luxembourg domestic law, no withholding tax is levied on interest or royalty payments to non-residents in respect of debt financing and IP licensing. Treaty rates are therefore generally irrelevant. Anti-abuse rules may superimpose a 15% withholding tax on excessive debt interest and royalties paid to entities in non-cooperative jurisdictions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: required when the aggregate value of related-party transactions exceeds €1,000,000 per fiscal year. Master File: required where the worldwide group consolidated revenue equals or exceeds €750,000,000. CbCR filing threshold: consolidated group revenue ≥ €750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg is not classified as an Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) jurisdiction. However, the Luxembourg Tax Administration applies substance-over-form under Art. 60a LIR (General Anti-Abuse Rule), ATAD 1/2, and administrative substance requirements for IP regimes. An SCSp must demonstrate substantive commercial activity in Luxembourg through local management decisions, physical office, qualified staff, local bank accounts, and effective operation of TikTok creator MCN agency services.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting TikTok creator revenue from the SCSp accounts, fabricating creator-advance deductions, diverting commission to shell intermediaries in zero-tax jurisdictions, or destroying financial records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Luxembourg Tax Adaptation Law (Steueranpassungsgesetz) §§ 186 ff., tax fraud is punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines up to €125,000. Civil penalties may reach 100% of the evaded tax, plus monthly late-payment interest at 0.8%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the general partner who participate in tax fraud are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax and interest. The Luxembourg tax administration may attach personal assets, apply for travel bans, and freeze bank accounts during criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying management fees, creator branding commissions, or data-syncing fees to a related Hong Kong, Singapore, or US affiliate at non-arm's-length amounts without a comparability analysis, or failing to prepare Local File documentation when related-party transactions exceed €1,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary TP adjustment reallocates profit to Luxembourg; secondary penalties may be up to 50% of the adjustment; late-payment interest accrues at 0.8% per month; administrative fines up to €250,000 may be imposed for non-compliance with documentation orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally assessed for gross negligence if they knowingly approved unbalanced intercompany pricing. Criminal liability arises only in cases of coordinated fraud, but civil claims for unpaid tax and interest can be pursued against the directors of the corporate general partner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing an SCSp without any Luxembourg substance, with no employees, no local management decisions, no office, and using the entity solely to route TikTok MCN income through Luxembourg for treaty benefits or participation-exemption advantages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Art. 60a LIR denies tax advantages where the main or one of the main purposes is tax avoidance. The entity may be disregarded for tax purposes; a 20–30% penalty of the tax advantage may be imposed; forced deregistration from the Luxembourg trade register (RCS) can follow.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the general partner can be held personally liable for the entity's tax debts if the entity is considered a sham. Travel bans may be ordered under Luxembourg administrative practice, and directors may be excluded from board positions in Luxembourg.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to perform customer due diligence on TikTok creators, commingling partner funds with agency operational funds, receiving payouts through unregulated crypto wallets or third-party payment rails without clear documentation, or failing to maintain anti-money-laundering policies under the Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Articles 8-1 and 8-2 of the amended Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF regulations, professional negligence is punishable with fines up to €1,250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years. Administrative fines may reach €1,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner who fail to implement AML/KYC controls face personal criminal liability, travel bans, and freezing of personal assets pending criminal proceedings. Reckless disregard can pierce the corporate veil, making directors personally liable for illicit fund flows.
